To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
screening for lung cancer is effective and should be offered to patients who meet the high-risk profile.

(1) screening with low-dosed computed tomography of asymptomatic persons at risk for lung cancer reduces mortality from lung cancer; (2) screening is associated with a small risk of radiation-induced lung cancer; (3) screening is associated only a modest increase in the detection of indolent lung cancers; and (4) screening is associated a modest increase in diagnostic procedures and procedures to treat benign conditions.
